item.title: Arthur Jafa, the Great Disrupter, Readies a ‘Big Bang’
item.description: “I Am Tony,” the artist’s largest museum survey to date, carries a powerful message about identity “forged in the holds of slave ships.”

item.title: Don’t Call Him Pop: A New, Improved Roy Lichtenstein Is at the Whitney
item.description: The artist Alex Da Corte and the curator Meg Onli bring fresh eyes to a survey bridging high art and mass culture. Will Lichtenstein resonate with a young audience?
item.dc:creator: Aruna D’Souza

item.title: Can Design Heal Battles on the Mall and the American College Campus?
item.description: Among this fall’s highlights: Memorials and a sculpture garden in Washington, a focus on pioneering Black architects, and design worth traveling for in Brussels and Mexico City.

item.category: Desert Shield and Desert Storm Memorial (Washington, DC)

item.title: Kent Monkman, an Indigenous Painter, Sees a Vermeer and the Sparks Fly
item.description: For a new show at the Frick Collection, Kent Monkman imagines what Indigenous people see when they see fur trappers, General Custer and even Jeff Bezos.
item.dc:creator: Zachary Small and Brendan George Ko
item.media:credit: Brendan George Ko for The New York Times

item.title: Did Trump Win the Battle Over the Smithsonian?
item.description: Lonnie G. Bunch III, who has led the institution since 2019, parried the White House until deciding it was time to go.
item.dc:creator: Robin Pogrebin
item.media:description: Mr. Bunch was named the secretary of the Smithsonian in 2019, during Mr. Trump’s first term.

item.title: How the Smithsonian Might Choose Its Next Leader
item.description: With Lonnie G. Bunch III stepping down as the Smithsonian’s secretary, President Trump will have his best chance to control the institution.
item.dc:creator: Robin Pogrebin
item.media:description: The Smithsonian Institution, the world’s largest museum, education and research complex, was created by Congress in 1846 and operates independently of the executive branch.

item.title: Unstitching the 1,000-Year-Old Story of the Bayeux Tapestry
item.description: The medieval masterpiece has traveled from France to England for a once-in-a-lifetime show. It is not what our critic Jason Farago expected.
item.dc:creator: Jason Farago

item.title: Lose Yourself in Yayoi Kusama’s Last Show
item.description: A landmark retrospective by the late Japanese artist invites visitors to surrender individual identity and step into an infinite cosmos.
item.dc:creator: Emily LaBarge
item.media:credit: Ilvy Njiokiktjien for The New York Times
item.media:description: “Infinity Mirrored Room — ‘The Hope of the Polka Dots Buried in Infinity Will Eternally Cover The Universe’” (2025) at the Stedelijk Museum in Amsterdam.

item.title: After Louvre Jewel Heist, Robberies Continue at French Museums
item.description: A spate of robberies, many in small towns, has raised questions about how to secure the country’s treasures.
item.dc:creator: Mark Landler
item.media:credit: Maeva Destombes/Hans Lucas, via Agence France-Presse — Getty Images
item.media:description: The Louvre’s Apollo Gallery, which housed royal jewels and crown diamonds.

item.title: Trump Demands Smithsonian Install ‘Colossus’ George Washington Statue
item.description: The president’s latest attack on the National Museum of American History reflects his longstanding desire for “patriotic” history.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer Schuessler
item.media:description: In a post on social media, President Trump also called for the Smithsonian’s National Museum of American History to host a five-year exhibition about Washington’s legacy “beginning now.”

item.title: Bayeux Tapestry Exhibition Opens at British Museum
item.description: On Thursday, the British Museum opened its blockbuster Bayeux Tapestry exhibition, its most eagerly anticipated show in decades.
item.dc:creator: Alex Marshall

item.title: Where to See the World’s Bayeux Tapestry Replicas
item.description: There are full-size replicas in a U.S. sports arena, an abbey in Denmark and a home in rural New Zealand. There’s even a more modest version for those who don’t like the original’s nudity.
item.dc:creator: Alex Marshall

item.title: An Artist Inspired by Men Behaving Badly
item.description: In a new show at David Kordansky Gallery, the Iranian American painter Tala Madani plumbs the lives of her characters with absurd humor and a strange tenderness.
item.dc:creator: Aruna D’Souza
item.media:credit: Maiwenn Raoult for The New York Times
item.media:description: The artist Tala Madani with “Disco-ball Break Out,” 2026. She paints the disco as a place where people indulge their impulses, sometimes with disastrous effects.

item.title: The Young Women at the Heart of American Landscape Art
item.description: Once dismissed as exercises in dainty femininity, the handiwork of schoolgirls is now celebrated for anticipating the art of the Hudson River School and beyond.
item.dc:creator: Celia McGee

item.title: Art Gallery Shows to See in September
item.description: This week in Newly Reviewed, Carolina Miranda covers Gronk’s coded paintings, Susan Silton’s violence and grief, and Urs Fischer’s charms.
item.dc:creator: Carolina A. Miranda and Will Heinrich

item.title: The Midcareer Artist Camille Henrot Is Apparently Tireless
item.description: The French artist makes you feel like a reveler in her epiphanies, from slapstick commedia dell’arte to dog sculptures in Central Park. At midcareer she is apparently tireless.
item.dc:creator: Walker Mimms
item.media:credit: Sam Hellmann for The New York Times

item.title: The Elusive Choreographer Sarah Michelson Is Turning MoMA Into a Dance Palace
item.description: Sarah Michelson presents her expansive vision of dance at the Museum of Modern Art, where she will take over the atrium in her exhibition, “nowhere.”
item.dc:creator: Gia Kourlas and Adam Golfer
item.media:description: “Dances are like embodied questions,” said the choreographer Sarah Michelson, center, here with, from left, Max Marxer, her studio assistant John Hoobyar and Mateo Tirres.

item.title: A Former Home for Pigeons, Refitted for People

item.title: Kennedy Center Warns of Bankruptcy Unless Trump’s Name Is Added
item.description: The caution, contained in a draft resolution to the center’s board, comes as a federal judge decides whether President Trump’s name should remain off the building.
item.dc:creator: Julia Jacobs
item.category: Kennedy, John F, Center for the Performing Arts
item.media:description: As a judge weighs whether President Trump’s name should be reinstalled on the Kennedy Center, its leaders say that, without such a move, it could soon be bankrupt.

item.title: Lonnie G. Bunch III, Departing Smithsonian Secretary, Faced ‘Mounting Pressure Campaign’
item.description: Under Lonnie G. Bunch III’s leadership, President Trump accused the Smithsonian of liberal, anti-American bias. Supporters say he was dedicated to nonpartisan scholarship.
